about.title: Clearlake Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Clearlake sits along a network of two-lane roads — Rt 53, Lakeshore Drive, Old Highway 53, and Olympic Drive — that carry local traffic through tight curves and shoreline stretches. Lake County's public collision records show 48 injury crashes and 74 injured people in the most recent final year, with Friday afternoons between 2 and 4 p.m. showing the heaviest reporting. If you were hurt in one of these collisions, the days right after matter. Photos, witness contacts, and vehicle damage can disappear or get harder to track down quickly. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm, that connects injured Clearlake residents with an independent personal injury attorney who can review the crash, handle communication with insurers, and explain your options. There's no obligation to move forward, and attorneys in this network work on contingency, meaning you owe nothing unless there's a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before Dealing With Insurance

items.title: California's Comparative Fault Rule
items.desc: Even if you're partly blamed for the crash, California's pure comparative fault law still lets you recover a share of damages. An attorney can help make sure the insurer isn't unfairly shifting blame onto you.

items.title: Recorded Statements Can Work Against You
items.desc: Insurance adjusters often ask for a recorded statement soon after a crash, and those words can later be used to reduce your claim. An attorney can speak for you and keep the process from working against your interests.

items.title: The Clock Is Shorter Than You Think
items.desc: California generally gives you two years to file an injury claim, but if a government entity (like a road authority) may be involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months. Getting evidence and legal advice early protects your options either way.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a Clearlake car accident?
items.answer: In most cases, California law gives you two years from the date of the crash to file a personal injury lawsuit. If your accident may involve a government-owned road or vehicle, that deadline can be much shorter, sometimes just six months. An attorney can help you figure out which timeline applies to your situation.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the crash?
items.answer: California follows a pure comparative fault system, which means you can still recover compensation even if you share some responsibility for the accident. Your recovery would simply be reduced by your percentage of fault. This is one reason it helps to have someone review the facts before you accept an insurer's version of events.

items.question: Why do so many crashes get reported around Friday afternoons in Clearlake?
items.answer: Public collision records for Clearlake show a pattern of higher reported crash activity on Fridays between roughly 2 and 4 p.m., often near corridors like Rt 53, Lakeshore Drive, and Olympic Drive. This is simply a pattern in the public data, not a judgment about any particular road. If your crash happened during this window, it may help to note the exact time and location for your attorney.

items.question: Does it cost anything to talk to an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service that connects you with an independent personal injury attorney, and there's no cost or obligation to see if it's a good fit. Attorneys in this network work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you recover compensation.
